newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai military won't help Hun Sen capture Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Thai military won't help Hun Sen capture Pol Pot.

text.p: Thailand's armed forces have no plans to comply with a request by Cambodian strongman Hun Sen to help capture Pol Pot, a Thai military spokesman said on Thursday.
"It is impossible for the Thai military to help Hun Sen capture Pol Pot," the general, who is a staff officer to prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, told Reuters.
"Pol Pot is in Cambodia and if Hun Sen really wants him, he should just send the troops to Anlong Veng and get him," he said.

He was responding to comments by Hun Sen in a television interview on Wednesday that he had a two-stage plan to gain control of the Anlong Veng area -- Pol Pot's headquarters -- through Khmer Rouge defections and "military measures".
He also said he would discuss with the Thai government the possibility of their cooperation in capturing Pol Pot and other Khmer Rouge officials.
But the Thai official said Bangkok would comply with measures adopted by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in dealing with Cambodia.

"If Hun Sen requires any assistance, he should tell the ASEAN ministers when they visit next week," he said. "Hun Sen should not unilaterally ask Thailand to take any initiative on the Pol Pot matter. Pol Pot is a dangerous and dirty object that nobody wants to touch."

Three ASEAN foreign ministers, including Thailand's Prachuab Chaiyasarn, were due to meet Hun Sen soon to try to help find a way to settle the political crisis in Cambodia caused when Hun Sen ousted his co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6.
Their previous efforts to mediate were rejected by Hun Sen.
Hun Sen made the comments about trying to capture Pol Pot after viewing a videotape of a show trial of the reviled Khmer Rouge leader in northern Cambodia last week.

In the trial, Pol Pot -- who is held responsible for the deaths of more than one million people during the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 "killing fields" rule -- was condemned and sentenced to life in detention for his crimes.
Thai officials have previously warned Ranariddh and other opposition politicians not to use Thai soil for a resistance movement and said they would not get involved in the Cambodian problem.
